outcome: The conjecture remains open, but the best known universal constant in the approximate form γ(G□H) ≥ c·γ(G)γ(H) was raised twice within the window: Steiner (arXiv:2606.14414, 2026-06-12) improved Clark & Suen's 2000 bound of 1/2 to (5+√73)/24 ≈ 0.5643, and Aliabadi & Krop (arXiv:2607.01109) then raised it further, first to ≈0.5809 (v1, 2026-07-01), then — after a withdrawn v2 flagged in the arXiv listing as containing an 'algebraic mistake' — to a corrected 2/3 ≈ 0.667 in v3 (2026-09-09). The claimed bipartite case-restriction preprint (arXiv:2509.10473, Hosking) and the Zenodo 'Impossible Descent' Lean 4 item do not add genuine progress (see summary).

ai.basis_quote: AI disclosure: During the preparation of this work, the authors used Claude (Fable 5) for language editing and computational assistance related to the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.

disputes.summary: Aliabadi & Krop v2 (posted 2026-07-02, one day after v1) was withdrawn; the arXiv math.CO July 2026 listing records the withdrawal comment 'Algebraic mistake.' v3 (2026-09-09) states the authors 'fixed the argument and made an improvement,' raising the claimed constant from v1's ≈0.5809 to 2/3. The v1 constant (0.5809) itself was never withdrawn or corrected — only v2 was pulled — so v1's result appears to stand as an intermediate step, superseded by v3's stronger 2/3 bound.

summary: Vizing's conjecture (γ(G□H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H) for all graphs G, H) is still open. Within the window, the universal-constant approximate form saw two genuine improvements: Raphael Steiner (arXiv:2606.14414, 2026-06-12, no AI mentioned) raised Clark & Suen's (2000) bound of 1/2 to (5+√73)/24 ≈ 0.5643 — the first improvement on that constant since 2000. Mohsen Aliabadi and Elliot Krop (arXiv:2607.01109) then improved it further: v1 (2026-07-01) claimed ≈0.5809 with no AI acknowledgement; v2 (2026-07-02) was withdrawn, flagged in the arXiv combinatorics listing as containing an 'algebraic mistake'; v3 (2026-09-09) fixed the argument, restructured the paper around Theorem 1.1 (a packing-based inequality) and Theorem 1.3 (the headline 2/3 bound), and carries an explicit AI disclosure that Claude (Fable 5) was used 'for language editing and computational assistance related to the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.' That sentence — the authors' own account, quoted directly from the v3 HTML — is the basis for `ai_role: assisted`: it names AI contribution to the derivation of specific numbered theorems, not merely proofreading or formalisation, so it clears the `none` bar. Neither of these bound-improvement papers has yet received an expert digestion (no Tao blog post, no Quanta coverage, no journal acceptance found); they remain unreviewed preprints, which is why status is `progress` rather than `claimed` — `claimed` per the rubric attaches to resolution/certificate claims, and a moved bound on a still-open problem is `progress` by definition regardless of review status. Separately, two lower-credibility items surfaced by triage were examined and found not to constitute progress: (1) arXiv:2509.10473 (Noah Hosking, math.GM, v1 2025-08-26 through v5 2026-08-23) does not prove the conjecture for any concrete case such as 'k-regular bipartite graphs with k≥7' as triage's note suggested — reading the full text shows it only proves a conditional inequality with an unresolved additive-deficit term (Remark 1), explicitly leaving the reduction to 'domination-neutral leaf deletions' as future work; it is math.GM (not math.CO), never rigorously closes any case, and so is not a genuine partial result. (2) The Zenodo item 'Vizing's Impossible Descent' (Jonathan Reed, posted 2026-08-08) claims a full Lean 4 proof by contradiction but is self-published with no corroboration, no peer engagement, and no visible acknowledgements section; per the rubric a machine-checked certificate no expert has reviewed would be `claimed` at best, but there is no evidence anyone besides the author has run or examined the Lean development, and no trace of it anywhere else (no arXiv cross-post, no mathoverflow/blog discussion), so it is treated as non-credible noise rather than a countable event, consistent with the triage note. I also checked arXiv:2608.29595 ('GPT, the Counterexample Machine' by Suvrit Sra), which surfaced in AI+Vizing search results; it documents ~16 GPT-discovered counterexamples in combinatorics/convexity/analysis but does not mention Vizing's conjecture at all — a false positive, not evidence for this record.
competing_reading: One could argue the Aliabadi-Krop v3 AI disclosure ('language editing and computational assistance related to the proofs') is ambiguous enough to read as `none` if 'computational assistance' meant only checking algebra rather than generating proof steps — the rubric's `none` bucket explicitly includes debugging and proofreading. I read 'computational assistance related to the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4' as naming a specific mathematical contribution to those theorems (not just language), which pushes it past the `none` threshold into `assisted`, but the sentence does not spell out exactly what Claude computed, so a stricter reading landing on `none` is defensible.
what_would_settle_it: The authors' full acknowledgement wording is already quoted in full above; what would resolve the ambiguity is the papers' actual working notes or a more detailed methods statement specifying whether Claude produced any algebraic step, inequality, or case analysis that appears in the final Theorem 1.1 / 1.4 proofs, versus merely double-checking arithmetic the authors had already derived.
